lead: Home and personal audio and video equipment, organised by what it does for sound or picture (headphones, speakers, record playing, amplifying, sources, portable players, radios, screens, smart speakers, accessories); enthusiast areas are broken into archetypes and versions, everyday screens and smart devices by what makes a good one.

depts.note: Tier for everyday wireless models; variety for the enthusiast (head-fi) end.
depts.t: Audio worn on or in the ears, wired or wireless, from hi-fi headphones to earbuds; spare parts and cables → Stands, cables & accessories; stage and studio monitoring gear → E3.
depts.ax: Does the sound unit sit around or on the ear, or go in or beside it?

s.t: Headphones with a band and two cups, from open hi-fi models to noise-cancelling travel sets and headsets; an earphone that goes in the ear → Earphones shelf.

k.a: circumaural headphones · full-size headphones · electrostatic headphones · Stax earspeakers
k.d: Headphone whose cups enclose the ear, open or sealed at the back, with a dynamic, planar-magnetic or electrostatic driver; electrostatic models need a separate energiser.

x.d: Sennheiser's open dynamic reference family that founded the enthusiast headphone hobby.
Large open dynamic flagship with angled drivers, Sennheiser's audiophile reference.
Beyerdynamic's first hi-fi headphones; semi-open DT 880 and open DT 990, in hi-fi, PRO and Edition forms.

v.d: semi-open; first dynamic headphone with electrostatic-like playback

x.d: High-end open headphone built on the Tesla driver system.
Semi-open studio headphone used by many recording studios for monitoring and playback.
Open reference headphone family widely used in studios; white K701, black K702 with removable cord.
Fully open former AKG flagship with drivers held away from the ear; no longer produced.
Large planar-magnetic open headphones that revived the planar type.
HiFiMAN's planar-magnetic flagships, from the hard-to-drive HE-6 to the Susvara (first shown as Edition 6, CES 2017).
Open dynamic flagship with 40 mm pure beryllium M-shaped dome drivers.
Koss's sealed stereo headphones that started hi-fi stereo headphone listening.
Closed monitoring headphone for recording studios, still widely used.
Closed member of Beyerdynamic's first hi-fi trio, standard studio and home closed-back.

v.d: PRO version with metal brackets; 80/250 ohm

x.d: Folding closed studio headphone that became an industry standard for engineers and broadcasting.
Closed professional monitor headphone with 45 mm drivers, Audio-Technica's best seller.
Bose's noise-cancelling headphone line, the long-running travel reference.
Sony's flagship wireless noise-cancelling headphone line, repeatedly top of independent tests.
Apple's over-ear wireless headphone with active noise cancellation and transparency mode.
Sennheiser's consumer headphone series, later wireless with noise cancelling.
Stax's first electrostatic earspeaker, the start of the type.
Rectangular-driver electrostatic earspeaker series, Stax's long-running core range.
Round-driver flagship electrostatic series.
Limited-edition electrostatic headphone system with its own amplifier; succeeded by the HE 1.
Cost-no-object electrostatic headphone system.

see: same headphones sold for studio monitoring

k.d: Headphone whose pads rest on the ear rather than around it, open or closed, such as the Grado SR and Sennheiser HD 25.

x.d: Lightweight on-ear headphone, called the world's first open-back headphone.
Portable high-end on-ear headphone in continuous production since 1984.
Grado's open on-ear headphones from the entry SR60 to the wooden RS1 and GS models.
Closed on-ear monitor headphone, a DJ-booth favourite.
Beats' best-selling fashion on-ear headphone line.

k.a: gaming headset · office headset · headphones with microphone
k.d: Headphones with a microphone attached, over or on the ear, for gaming, calls or streaming.
see: a different object: the bearing set of a bicycle

s.t: Units that sit in or beside the ear, from wired earbuds and moulded monitors to true wireless buds and bone-conduction sets; a band-and-cup headphone → Headphones shelf.

k.d: Earphone that rests in the outer ear without sealing the canal, wired.

x.d: Apple's bundled white wired earbuds, round from 2001 and contoured EarPods from 2012.

k.d: Earphone that seals the ear canal with standard tips, sold for listening.

x.d: Single balanced-armature, deep-insertion earphone; the first hi-fi noise-isolating in-ear.
Sound-isolating stage and listening earphones with detachable cables, from single dynamic to quad armature.
Electrostatic in-ear system with its own energiser.
Single 7 mm driver audiophile in-ears in plastic, zirconium and aluminium housings.
Five-armature IEM in a green aluminium shell, revised many times.
Multi-driver universal IEMs with tubeless tia armatures and APEX pressure vents.
Hybrid IEM regarded as the benchmark at its price, much imitated in Chi-Fi.
Budget 1DD + 3BA hybrid tuned close to the Blessing 2.

see: the same earphones used on stage and in the studio

k.d: In-ear earphones with shells moulded to one listener's ear canal.

x.d: Jerry Harvey's later multi-driver custom monitors with integrated crossovers.
Custom-shell versions of 64 Audio's tia monitors.

see: stage and studio use of custom moulds

k.d: Two separate wireless buds sold with a charging case.

x.d: Apple's wireless earbuds, the best-selling true wireless line.
Sealing AirPods with active noise cancellation.
Sony's flagship noise-cancelling true wireless earbuds.
Samsung's true wireless earbud series, successor to the Gear IconX.
Bose's noise-cancelling true wireless earbuds.

k.d: Earphones that leave the ear canal open, by bone conduction or an open-ear driver.

x.d: Wrap-around bone-conduction sports headphone, Shokz's flagship line.
Entry-level bone-conduction headphone of Shokz's Open series.
Waterproof bone-conduction headphone with built-in MP3 player, first sold as Xtrainerz.

s.ax: kinds by how the unit sits: outer ear, sealed canal, moulded canal, cordless in the canal, outside the canal

depts.note: Variety for hi-fi loudspeakers; tier for home-cinema, soundbars and wireless speakers.
depts.t: Speakers that turn an amplifier or wireless signal into room sound, from hi-fi to surround to soundbars; a speaker run by an assistant → Smart speakers & displays; a stage PA speaker → E3.
depts.ax: What system is the speaker made for: stereo listening, a surround layout, or self-contained TV and wireless use?

s.t: Speakers for two-channel listening, from stand-mounted monitors and floor-standers to panel, horn and single-driver designs; a surround channel speaker → Home cinema speakers.

k.d: Compact speaker cabinet made to stand on a stand, shelf or desk, passive or active.

x.d: BBC-designed miniature monitor for outside-broadcast vans, built under licence by many makers.
x.dt: 15 or 11 ohm · KEF B110 and T27 drivers · veneer

x.d: Two-way sealed bookshelf speaker with white-cone woofer that became a nearfield studio monitor.
Bextrene-cone BBC-school monitor by Spencer Hughes, made until 1994 and reborn in the Classic range.
First Harbeth speaker, with Dudley Harwood's patented polypropylene cone.
Sealed acoustic-suspension speakers that made deep bass possible from a small box.
Henry Kloss's affordable two-way with a 10-inch woofer, later called the Larger Advent.
Three-way control monitor and its 1970s best-selling home version.
Very small two-way monitor designed in 1976, made in many versions.
50th-anniversary Uni-Q coaxial standmount that brought the LS3/5A idea into the living room.
Small two-way bookshelf speaker that launched the Diamond range as a budget hi-fi benchmark.
x.dt: compact two-way · now in its twelfth generation

k.d: Tall speaker cabinet that stands on the floor.

x.d: Flagship three-way monitor line used at Abbey Road, from the 801 to the Diamond-tweeter 800D.
Spiral-shell four-way flagship with tapered-tube driver loading.
Floor-standing speaker using Linn's patented isobaric bass loading.
Tiny monitor (WATT) on a bass module (Puppy) that became the best-known high-end floor system.
Wilson's modular cost-no-object flagships.
Direct/reflecting speaker with nine 4.5-inch drivers and an active equaliser.
Single Apparent Source flagship with Uni-Q and force-cancelling woofers.
Tannoy's flagship home range built around its Dual Concentric driver, tweeter behind the bass cone.
Long-running Dynaudio series of stand-mount, floorstanding and centre speakers.

k.d: Speaker that reproduces only bass, for stereo or surround systems.
see: a subwoofer is the .1 of a surround layout

k.a: electrostat · panel speaker · magnetostatic · ribbon speaker
k.d: Loudspeaker driven by a large thin film panel, electrostatic or planar-magnetic, usually radiating front and back.

x.d: First production full-range electrostatic loudspeaker.
Thin dipole planar-magnetic panels from Minnesota.
Curved CLS electrostatic panels joined to dynamic woofers.
Electrostatic mid/treble panel on a conventional bass unit.

k.d: Home loudspeaker whose drivers fire through horns for high efficiency, often suited to low-power valve amplifiers.

x.d: Three-way corner horn using the room walls as horn extensions, made in Hope, Arkansas since 1946.
Klipsch's horn-loaded siblings of the Klipschorn.

x.n: Altec Lansing Voice of the Theatre
x.d: Two-way cinema horn systems later used in studios and homes.
Spherical-horn speakers with active woofers: two-way Duo and three-way Trio.

k.d: Loudspeaker built around one wide-range driver with no crossover, often in a horn, baffle or transmission-line cabinet.

s.ax: kinds by cabinet role first (stand-mount, floor-standing, bass-only), then by driver principle (panel, horn, single driver)

s.t: Speakers sold for a surround layout, as a package or by position in the room; a stereo pair for music → Hi-fi loudspeakers.

k.a: Home cinema speaker system · Centre speaker · Surround speakers · In-wall speakers · On-wall speakers
k.d: Matched set of speakers sold together for a surround layout, with or without a subwoofer.
m: Polk Audio Signature Elite 5.2 Home Theater System
see: a soundbar is the one-box alternative

k.d: Speaker placed under or behind the screen to carry dialogue in a surround layout.
Speaker placed at the sides or rear of the room for the surround channels, on a stand, shelf or wall.
Speaker for the overhead channels of an object-based surround layout, upward-firing or ceiling-mounted.
Speaker made to be built into a wall or ceiling, with a grille flush to the surface; the installed fitting belongs with the home.
see: the same speaker as a fitted part of the home

s.ax: kinds by place in the layout: the whole package, centre, sides and rear, overhead, built into the wall

s.t: Self-contained speakers that need no separate amplifier: a bar under the TV, a mains-powered Wi-Fi speaker, a battery speaker to carry; a speaker with a voice assistant → Smart speakers & displays.

k.d: Speaker made as a bar for a TV, with or without a separate subwoofer.
m: Polk Audio MagniFi Max AX SR

k.a: wireless home speaker · smart speaker (Sonos type) · single-enclosure speaker
k.d: Mains-powered speaker that streams over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth, often grouping with others across rooms.
see: a speaker run by a voice assistant

k.d: Battery-powered speaker made to carry around, usually Bluetooth and often waterproof; party speakers are the largest.
see: a portable system with its own player

depts.note: Turntable, tonearm, cartridge and phono stage kept together as the vinyl chain.
depts.t: Gear for playing vinyl and shellac records, from the player to the pickup and the stage after it; the records themselves → F1; a DJ deck → E3.
depts.ax: Which link in the record-playing chain is it: the player, the arm, the pickup or the stage after it?

s.t: Machines that spin a record and track the groove, from acoustic gramophones and all-in-one players to hi-fi turntable decks; the radio-and-record cabinet → Radios & music systems.

k.d: Acoustic or early electric record player that plays wax cylinders or shellac discs through a horn, from Edison's phonograph to the wind-up gramophone.

x.d: Victor's cabinet gramophone with the horn hidden inside, sold as a piece of furniture; electrical Orthophonic models followed in 1925.

v.d: played the new electrically recorded discs

k.a: record player · portable record player · suitcase turntable
k.d: Complete electric record player with built-in speakers, in a suitcase, console or compact case, needing no separate amplifier.

x.d: Early all-transistor portable record player for 45 rpm discs.

see: a record player in a furniture cabinet with a radio

k.d: Record-playing deck with platter and tonearm, sold without amplifier or speakers.

x.d: Idler-drive transcription turntables, now prized for restoration in heavy plinths.

v.d: first transcription deck for 33, 45 and 78 rpm

x.d: Swiss transcription turntable made 1957–1965, a collector classic.
Broadcast studio turntable with idler-wheel drive and large platter for 16-inch transcription discs.

v.d: Smaller sibling keeping the idler-wheel drive
Belt-drive design based on the Thorens TD125

x.d: Swiss-origin turntable made for almost two decades; an enthusiast base for custom plinths.
Belt-driven suspended sub-chassis decks that set the pattern for later British designs.
Low-cost belt-drive deck with suspended platter and sub-chassis, ancestor of the LP12.
Suspended sub-chassis belt-drive deck, upgraded piece by piece for fifty years.
x.dt: arm (Ittok, Ekos, Akito, Basik) · plinth wood · power supply level

x.d: Quartz-locked direct-drive turntable; the MK2 became the DJ standard.
First direct-drive turntable on the professional market, sold as a drive unit without arm or plinth.
Tangential-arm turntable, later restored by B&O as a recreated edition.
Acrylic-plinth suspended deck with gold platter weights.
Very heavy Japanese reference turntable sold as a separate drive unit (RY-5500) without tonearm.
Light, rigid British belt-drive decks with Rega arms; the Planar 3 is the best known.
Budget belt-drive deck credited with helping the vinyl revival.

see: a direct-drive deck built for mixing

s.ax: kinds from the earliest to the hi-fi separate: acoustic machine, all-in-one electric player, turntable deck

s.t: Parts that carry the cartridge or hold the deck, sold for upgrades: tonearms, headshells and plinths; the cartridge itself → Cartridges & styli.

k.d: Base or chassis made to hold one turntable mechanism and its tonearm, sold separately.
Arm that carries the cartridge across the record, sold separately for a turntable.

x.d: SME's first arms, 9- and 12-inch, the standard of the 1960s and 1970s.
Linn's first own-badge arm (1979–1993), succeeded by the Ekos.
One-piece cast arms fitted to Rega decks and supplied to other makers.

k.d: Removable carrier at the end of the tonearm that holds the cartridge.

s.ax: kinds from the base up to the pickup: plinth, arm, headshell

s.t: The pickup that reads the groove and the tip that wears out: moving-magnet and moving-coil cartridges, and replacement styli.

k.d: Pickup cartridge made to fit a turntable tonearm.

x.d: The first Stereo Pick-Up, a moving-coil cartridge still made in headshell form.
Low-output moving-coil cartridge developed with Japan's NHK for broadcast use.
Moving-magnet cartridge series with a Micro-Ridge stylus, widely used as a benchmark.
Integrated-headshell DJ pickup.
Moving-magnet series with interchangeable styli, colour-coded by grade.
Entry moving-magnet cartridge made for 38 years, replaced in 2018 by the VM95 family sharing one body.
DJ moving-magnet cartridge; Shure left the phono market in 2018.
High-output cartridges in ½-inch and P-mount with user-replaceable styli.

see: a cartridge built for scratching and cueing

k.d: Replacement stylus made for a phono cartridge.

s.t: What happens to the signal and the record around the deck: phono preamplifiers and record-cleaning machines.

k.d: Stage that raises and equalises a phono cartridge signal to line level.
Machine that washes vinyl records and removes the fluid, by vacuum or ultrasonic bath.

depts.note: Variety for stereo hi-fi including vintage; tier for AV gear.
depts.t: Boxes that amplify, convert or decode sound for speakers and headphones; an instrument amplifier → E3; a set with speakers built in → Radios & music systems.
depts.ax: What does the box do to the signal: amplify it for speakers, convert digital audio for headphones, or decode it for surround?

s.t: Two-channel amplifiers from all-in-one receivers to separate preamplifier and power stages, such as the Marantz 2270, Quad II and McIntosh MC275; a surround amplifier → Home cinema electronics.

k.d: Stereo amplifier with a built-in radio tuner.

x.d: 1970s Marantz stereo receivers with silver fronts and blue-lit dials, a vintage collector favourite.
Flagship AM/FM receiver rated 270 W per channel, among the most powerful receivers made.
Sansui flagship stereo receiver with Dolby noise reduction.

k.d: Stereo amplifier with preamplifier and power stage in one box.

x.d: Integrated amplifier with a switch between class A and class B output; began Yamaha's 1970s CA line.
Black-faced Sansui integrated amplifiers made from 1965, a vintage collector line.
Yamaha integrated amplifiers from the A-1 onwards.
Low-cost integrated amplifier designed by Bjørn Erik Edvardsen, NAD's most famous product.
The first product of A&R Cambridge (Arcam), a British budget integrated amplifier.
Naim's first integrated amplifier, a small minimalist design.
Small half-width integrated amplifier that began the Cyrus range under Mission.
Budget integrated amplifier whose sound was based on the Leak Stereo 20 valve amplifier.
McIntosh integrated amplifiers with blue output meters, including hybrid valve/solid-state models.
Accuphase integrated amplifiers, from the E-202 onwards.

see: the same amplifier with a radio tuner added

k.d: Control and switching stage that feeds a separate power amplifier.

x.d: Valve stereo preamplifier that sold over 130,000 units; follows Saul Marantz's Model 1.
McIntosh preamplifiers, valve and solid-state.
Early Mark Levinson solid-state preamplifiers designed by John Curl.
One of Kensonic (Accuphase)'s first products, reviewed in 1973–74.
Luxman flagship preamplifier paired with the M-05.

k.d: Amplifier stage that drives speakers from a preamplifier signal, stereo or one channel per box.

x.d: Leak valve amplifiers claiming under 0.1% distortion; the TL/12 became a BBC standard.

v.d: basis of the Rega Brio's sound

x.d: Valve mono power amplifier made 1953–1970, often paired with the Quad ESL.
Stereo valve power amplifier with two pairs of EL34 per channel, 35 W per channel.
70 W valve monoblock power amplifier.
Stereo valve power amplifier with McIntosh's Unity Coupled Circuit, still in production.
300 W per channel solid-state amplifier used in the Grateful Dead's Wall of Sound.
Naim's stereo power amplifier, launched 1975.
25 W class A mono power amplifier.
Nelson Pass's Threshold amplifiers, later built under licence by Nakamichi.
Single-ended class A amplifiers by Nelson Pass.

x.n: Pass Labs X and XA series
x.d: Pass Labs amplifiers using the supersymmetry topology; XA adds Aleph-style class A.
One of Kensonic (Accuphase)'s first products.
Luxman flagship power amplifier paired with the C-05.

k.a: sound processor · graphic equaliser · parametric equaliser
k.d: Stereo component for shaping the tone or sound field of a signal.

x.d: 10-band graphic equaliser with a slider per band.

s.ax: kinds by how many stages share a box: tuner, preamplifier and power together; preamplifier and power; each alone; tone shaping

s.t: Boxes that turn digital audio into analogue and drive headphones, such as the Chord Mojo and Schiit Bifrost; a headphone or earphone → Headphones & earphones.

k.d: External device whose designed function is converting digital audio to analogue.

x.d: British high-end converters built on dCS's own Ring DAC; Elgar was its first consumer DAC.

v.d: first dCS with a headphone output

x.d: Converter from a studio-equipment maker that became an audiophile reference.
Standalone DAC derived from the Hugo 2 without battery or headphone output.
User-upgradable DAC, Schiit's first.

m: FiiO Warmer Desktop R2R Tube Buffer and DAC

k.a: DAC/amp combo · USB DAC dongle · portable DAC/amp
k.d: External device that converts digital audio and drives headphones in one unit.

x.d: Chord's FPGA-based DAC/headphone amplifiers with Rob Watts's filter code, from pocket Mojo to desktop Hugo TT.
Studio-maker DAC with headphone and IEM outputs and five-band parametric EQ; a simplified ADI-2 Pro.

k.d: External device whose designed function is amplifying a headphone signal.

x.d: Open-source headphone amplifier by the anonymous engineer NwAvGuy, built and sold by several firms.
Popular DIY op-amp headphone amplifier small enough to fit in a mint tin.
Schiit's first headphone amplifiers, which started the company.
Hand-built all-valve single-ended OTL headphone amplifier with 6AS7/6080 power valves.
Headphone amplifier using two 6922 valves.
Valve headphone amplifier.

k.a: Bluetooth audio transmitter · Bluetooth audio receiver
k.d: External unit that sends audio from a TV or player to wireless headphones or speakers, or receives Bluetooth audio into a hi-fi.

s.ax: kinds by what the box does: convert only, convert and drive headphones, drive headphones only, bridge to wireless

s.t: Boxes that decode and amplify surround sound and switch video, such as the Denon AVR-X range and Trinnov Altitude; a stereo amplifier → Stereo amplifiers & receivers.

k.d: Multichannel amplifier with surround decoding, video switching and a tuner in one box.
Multichannel surround preamplifier and decoder that feeds separate power amplifiers.
see: the same decoding with amplifiers built in

depts.note: Variety for tape and vintage decks (period view); tier for modern disc and streaming sources.
depts.t: Hi-fi components that read tape, discs or a network stream and send the signal to an amplifier; the media themselves → F1; a record deck → Turntables & vinyl playback.
depts.ax: What carries the music into the system: tape, a disc, or a network or radio signal?

s.t: Components that play and record magnetic tape, from open reel to cassette to digital tape, such as the Revox A77, Nakamichi Dragon and Sony DTC-60ES.

k.d: Hi-fi component that plays and records open-reel magnetic tape.

x.d: Swiss transistor open-reel recorders with servo direct-drive capstan; over 460,000 A77s were built.
Willi Studer's first Revox valve recorders.
Four-track home recorder with Simul-Sync overdubbing, popular with musicians.
Popular Akai open-reel decks with GX glass-ferrite heads.
Pioneer open-reel deck reviewed in 1977–78.
Sony open-reel deck typical of a 1970s audiophile machine.

k.d: Home component that plays (and may record) 8-track tape cartridges; an 8-track player fitted in a car is in Vehicles.
Hi-fi component that plays and records compact cassettes.

x.d: The first high-fidelity cassette deck, pairing Dolby B with chromium dioxide tape.
Three-head, dual-capstan decks that set the standard for cassette fidelity.
x.dt: head count · Dolby B/C · metal-tape capability

x.d: Top Nakamichi deck with motor-driven automatic azimuth correction (NAAC), made 1983–1995.
Auto-reverse decks that mechanically eject and flip the cassette (UDAR).
Four-motor, beltless direct-drive cassette deck made 1985–1992.
High-end Tandberg decks with automatic bias and head azimuth adjustment.
Akai closed-loop three-head decks with glass-and-crystal ferrite heads.

k.d: Hi-fi component that plays and records digital audio tape (DAT) cassettes.

s.ax: kinds by tape format, from open reel to cartridge to cassette to digital tape

s.t: Components that play or record optical and magneto-optical discs, such as the Sony CDP-101 and Sony MDS-JE780.

k.a: compact disc player · CD transport · SACD player
k.d: Player for compact discs.

x.d: The first commercially released CD player, on sale in Japan from October 1982.
Philips's first CD player, on sale in the US and Europe from March 1983.
Described as the first audiophile CD player.
Marantz's iconic CD player range, much modified by enthusiasts.
Naim's top CD player, announced 1989.
Linn's CD players, made until it switched to streaming in 2009.
CD player heavily based on the Studer A725 and A727.

k.d: Hi-fi component that plays and records MiniDiscs.

x.d: Sony home MiniDisc deck made 2002–2005.

k.d: Hi-fi component that records audio onto recordable compact discs from other sources.

s.t: Components that take the music from the internet, the home network or the air, such as the Linn DS and Quad FM3.

k.a: music streamer · network player · music server
k.d: Hi-fi source that plays music from the network or streaming services into an audio system.

x.d: Linn's network streamers; the Klimax DS (2007) launched its streaming strategy.
Network music players from Slim Devices, bought by Logitech in 2006; discontinued 2012.
Naim's range of one-box streaming players and amplifiers.
Media server system Meridian gained by buying Sooloos in 2008.

k.d: Hi-fi separate that receives radio broadcasts for an amplifier, with no speaker of its own.

x.d: Valve FM tuner designed with Richard Sequerra, a collector icon.
Quad FM tuner, made 1971–1982.
One of Kensonic (Accuphase)'s first products.
Revox synthesiser FM tuner.
Naim's top FM tuner, developed by Guy Lamotte.

depts.note: Personal players with a strong collector following, plus portable radio-cassettes.
depts.t: Battery-powered players you carry: headphone players from the Walkman to the iPod, and boomboxes with speakers; a speaker without a player → Loudspeakers; a phone → D2.
depts.ax: Is the music heard through headphones or through speakers built into the unit?

s.t: Pocket players made for headphones, such as the Sony Walkman, Discman, MiniDisc Walkman and Apple iPod; a boombox with speakers → Boombox shelf.

k.d: Battery-powered personal player for compact cassettes, listened to through headphones; hi-fi tape decks are a separate kind.

x.d: The first low-cost personal stereo; its name became the generic word for the type.
x.dt: playback or record · radio · Dolby · auto-reverse · colour

x.d: Metal-cased portable cassette recorder with hi-fi deck performance, used for field and radio recording.

v.d: line in/out, Dolby B and C; made to 2003

x.d: Aiwa personal cassette player series, a main rival to the Sony Walkman.
Toshiba cassette player line; the KT-AS10 has a removable cassette-shaped radio tuner.
Panasonic personal stereo cassette player series.

k.d: Battery-powered personal player for compact discs, listened to through headphones; hi-fi CD players are a separate kind.

x.d: First portable CD player, about half the price of Sony's first home CD player; renamed CD Walkman by 2000.

k.d: Battery-powered personal player or recorder for MiniDisc, a rewritable magneto-optical disc format sold 1992–2013.

x.d: Sony's MiniDisc players and recorders, from the first MZ-1 to the Hi-MD MZ-RH1.

v.d: Hi-MD; last MiniDisc Walkman, made to 2011

x.dt: player or recorder · NetMD · Hi-MD · colour

k.a: digital audio player · DAP · portable media player
k.d: Portable device sold mainly to play stored or streamed music, with no calling.

x.d: First commercially successful portable MP3 player; survived an RIAA lawsuit.
Hard-drive music player using laptop drives; the line became the Creative Zen.
Apple's music player line, 2001–2022, from the hard-drive click-wheel original to the touchscreen iPod touch.
Hard-drive players with optical output and FM tuner, a favourite for Rockbox firmware.
Microsoft's iPod rival with wireless sharing, sold 2006–2011.
Sony's flash-memory Walkman players, now high-resolution players in A, ZX and WM1 series.
First flash-memory MP3 player, sold in South Korea from 1998 and in North America as the EigerMan.
First hard-drive MP3 player, developed by Hango Electronics and sold by Compaq.
Hard-drive MP3 player that rivalled the Creative Nomad Jukebox.

k.d: Pocket device that plays video and photos as well as music from its own storage, without calling.

x.d: The first portable media player, with a colour screen for video.

s.ax: kinds by what holds the music: cassette, compact disc, MiniDisc, memory, memory with a video screen

s.t: Carry-handle systems with their own speakers, such as the Philips Radiorecorder and JVC RC-M90; a Bluetooth speaker with no player → Soundbars & wireless speakers.

k.d: Portable radio-cassette or CD system with built-in speakers and a carry handle.

x.d: Philips, inventor of the compact cassette, made the first boombox.
Huge six-speaker radio-cassette called the king of the boomboxes, used in music battles.
One of the 'boombox kings' used in music battles.
Upside-down-layout radio-cassette with two 8-inch speakers and 5-band equaliser.
Onkyo off-brand radio-cassette carried by Schoolly D.

depts.note: Variety for vintage radios, radiograms and jukeboxes; tier for everyday radios and compact systems.
depts.t: Sets that receive broadcasts, and cabinet, coin or shelf machines that play recorded music; a hi-fi tuner → Hi-fi sources; two-way and amateur radio → D2.
depts.ax: Does it only receive broadcasts, or does it also play recorded music?

s.t: Broadcast receivers with a built-in speaker, from valve table sets and transistor portables to shortwave and crystal radios.

k.a: tabletop radio · valve radio · DAB radio
k.d: Mains or battery radio with a built-in speaker, made to stand on a shelf or table.

x.d: Round Bakelite table radio by architect Wells Coates, an Art Deco design classic.
Philips valve table radios with separate bass and treble output stages and two speakers.
Leatherette-covered British portable whose 1950s look returned as the Roberts Revival.

ax: What does the equipment do for sound or picture: go on the ear, fill a room, play records, amplify, feed a hi-fi, travel with you, receive broadcasts, show a picture, answer a voice, or support the rest?
key: 1. Is it a stand, mount, cable, aerial, remote or spare part made for other audio or video gear? → Stands, cables & accessories
2. Is it worn on or in the ears? → Headphones & earphones
3. Is it a speaker, screen or hub run by a voice assistant? → Smart speakers & displays
4. Does it show a picture, throw one onto a surface, or feed one to a screen? → TVs, projectors & video players
5. Does it play records or belong to the record-playing chain (deck, arm, pickup, phono stage, record cleaner)? → Turntables & vinyl playback
6. Is it a battery player you carry, or a boombox with its own speakers? → Portable audio
7. Does it receive broadcasts with its own speaker, or play records, discs or coins from a cabinet or shelf system? → Radios & music systems
8. Is it a box that amplifies, converts or decodes sound for speakers or headphones? → Amplifiers & electronics
9. Is it a component that reads tape, a disc or a network stream and sends it to an amplifier? → Hi-fi sources: tape, disc & streaming
10. Is it a speaker, soundbar or subwoofer? → Loudspeakers

Precedence: a smart speaker is step 3 before a loudspeaker (step 10); a boombox or radio-cassette is step 6 before a loudspeaker; a receiver with a tuner is step 8, a stand-alone tuner step 9; a radiogram is step 7 before a turntable (step 5).
